To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
informing women about the harms and benefits of screening using mammograms has no impact on informed choice and decisional conflict.

informing about the benefits of screening and harms of overdiagnosis and overtreatment in women facing the invitation to participate for the first time in breast cancer screening with mammography does not increase informed choice, decisional conflict, or anxiety.

(1) the provision of information about benefits and harms of a screening test to women who are approaching the age of being invited to mammography screening increases their knowledge, reduces their decisional conflict and their anxiety and worry about breast cancer, and increases their confidence in the decision and their intention of being screened.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of information about the harms and benefits of screening in women’s decision-making.
the effect of information about benefits and harms of the BCSP on informed choice in Spanish women approaching the age to participate in screening.
the effects of informing women of the benefits and harms in breast cancer screening using mammography.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the InforMa study has been designed to assess the impact on women of receiving a leaflet that provides information about the benefits, harms, and risks of screening for breast cancer.
this trial is the first RCDM study that assesses the impact of informing women about the benefits and the harms of breast cancer mammography screening on decisional outcomes.

the InforMa study is an ongoing RCT that aims to assess the effect of informing women about the benefits and the harms of mammography screening on informed choice, decisional conflict, anxiety about screening participation, and several other outcomes in women approaching the decision to be invited to mammography screening.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are conducting a randomized controlled trial to assess the effects, in terms of decision-making and other outcomes, of receiving information about breast cancer screening using mammography in women approaching the invitation to participate.
it will provide information on the effects of informing about the harms of breast cancer on decision-making in Spain.
it will be a study of the effect on informed choice of providing information on the benefits, and harms, of screening using mammograms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
women who received the information on the benefits, harms and uncertainties about mammography were more informed and had less decisional conflict than women in the control group.
women want to know about both benefits and harms of the screening program, and this information should be provided.
providing women with detailed information on benefits and harms of the screening program is not enough to achieve informed choice.
